title: Scientists often model Mars’s interior as a set of uniform spherical layers, but 16 years of tracking data from three NASA orbiters reveals something radically uneven: the mantle beneath the southern highlands may be up to 720 degrees Fahrenheit hotter than beneath the northern lowlands—and researchers still don’t know whether persistent mantle upwelling, an insulating crust or the after-effects of an ancient giant impact created it.
description: Seasonal changes in Mars's gravity imply that the mantle beneath its ancient southern highlands is hundreds of degrees warmer than the north, but three origin stories remain.
